Meeting and chat assignment, round robin or direct
Test meeting and chat record

steps: Connect the Meeting Booking and Live Chat integrations in Composer, so the concierge can check availability, start a chat and book a slot.
Set the Handoff to sales skill's conditions and instructions for your business, agreed with your sales leads.
Test the handoff in preview, with a representative taking the chat and the booking, and adjust the conditions until it works as agreed.
Walk your representatives through the chat inbox and the conversation score, then publish.
deliverables: Meeting Booking and Live Chat integrations connected in Composer
Handoff to sales skill set for your business
Preview test record
Representative walkthrough of the chat inbox

outcome: Your concierge can check availability, start a live chat and book a meeting slot, handing visitors to your representatives when your agreed conditions are met.

steps: Agree with your sales leads which team takes which visitors, by geography, product interest, company size or industry.
Build the routing rules in Adobe Marketo Qualifier on the visitor's Marketo lead and company attributes, and set each rule's priority and representatives.
Test the rules with sample visitors for each route, including visitors who match more than one rule, and record the results.
deliverables: Routing rules with priorities and representatives
Routing map agreed with your sales leads
Sample visitor test results
asks: Your sales coverage by geography, product, company size or industry
The representatives who belong to each team
risk: A visitor routed to the wrong team when rules overlap: we set each rule's priority and test with sample visitors who match more than one rule.
outcome: Concierge visitors who ask for a person reach the right team by geography, product interest, company size or industry, based on their Marketo attributes.

steps: Agree with your sales leads which Marketo activities representatives should see, such as email opens and clicks, web visits and form fills.
Create the API credentials in the Adobe Developer Console, and set up the webhook in Marketo Engage using Adobe's payload template, matched to your field names.
Add the webhook to the trigger Smart Campaigns for the agreed activities.
Generate each agreed activity on a test prospect, and check that it arrives under Marketing Highlights in Marketo Qualifier.
deliverables: API credentials and Marketo Engage webhook
Trigger Smart Campaigns for the agreed activities
Test record of activity in Marketing Highlights
asks: A Marketo Engage administrator to set up the webhook and campaigns with us
Access to the Adobe Developer Console for your organization
risk: Activity that never reaches representatives because field names differ: we match the payload template to your instance's field names and test each activity on a test prospect.
outcome: Your representatives see each prospect's live Marketo activity under Marketing Highlights, and can filter prospects by it.

steps: Check that activity sync is on, and that Marketo Qualifier's email sent, opened, clicked and replied activities arrive in Marketo Engage.
Agree with your marketing team how its programs treat prospects in active outreach, and record the rules.
Add the outreach activities to your Marketo Engage lead scoring and engagement programs, following the agreed rules.
Test with sample prospects, and check that their scores and engagement timelines show the outreach activities as agreed.
deliverables: Outreach activities synced into Marketo Engage
Agreed rules for prospects in active outreach
Updated lead scoring and engagement programs
Sample prospect test results
asks: Your marketing team's view on how programs should treat prospects in active outreach
A Marketo Engage administrator to update scoring and programs with us
risk: Marketing emails landing on prospects a representative is already contacting: we agree how programs treat active outreach first and test with sample prospects.
outcome: Your sales outreach counts in Marketo Engage lead scoring and engagement timelines, and your programs treat prospects in active outreach as your teams agreed.

steps: Agree with your sales leads which live Marketo activity should enroll a prospect, and in which Outbound Workflow.
Set the targeting criteria on each Outbound Workflow, so matching prospects are enrolled for the representative who owns them.
Check owner matching against your CRM for a sample of prospects, and list any mismatches for your CRM team to correct.
Test enrollment with sample activity, including the warning for prospects another representative is already contacting.
deliverables: Targeting criteria on your Outbound Workflows
Owner matching check against your CRM
Enrollment and warning test results
asks: Your sales leads' rules for which activity should start outreach
A CRM contact to correct owner records that do not match
risk: Prospects enrolled for the wrong representative: we check owner matching against your CRM before go-live and test the warning for prospects already in contact.
outcome: Prospects whose live Marketo activity matches your criteria are enrolled in Outbound Workflows for the representative who owns them, with a warning when another is already contacting them.

steps: Agree with your planners and asset team which Planning record types, such as campaigns and products, connect to which AEM Assets objects.
Connect the agreed record types to AEM Assets images, folders and Content Fragments.
Link the first campaigns and products to their content, and check that each record is linked to the right images, folders or Content Fragments.
Write a short guide for your planners on linking new records to their content, and walk them through it.
deliverables: Record types connected to AEM Assets
First campaigns and products linked to their content
Planner guide to linking records

outcome: Your plans in Workfront Planning link to the images, folders and Content Fragments in AEM Assets that belong to them.

steps: Agree with your planners and asset team which Planning record fields assets should carry, such as campaign, product and region.
Add matching fields to an AEM Assets metadata form, so the values show on each asset's details page.
Configure the metadata mapping through the Workfront and AEM Assets integration, with your Workfront administrator.
Check a sample of assets from each record type, making sure campaign, product and region match the plan.

Metadata form fields in AEM Assets
Sample check results

The plan fields your teams want on each asset

outcome: Your assets in AEM Assets carry campaign, product and region from the plan, so your teams can find them by the details they plan with.

steps: Agree with your Workfront administrator which access levels get the Coworker panel, and which Read-only and Write-only MCP tools to select.
Have your administrator enable Coworker, select the agreed tools in the System Preferences area of Setup, and allow the panel in those access levels.
Test with users at each access level, checking that Coworker acts only within each user's Planning permissions and waits for a yes before changing records.
deliverables: Coworker enabled with the agreed MCP tools
Coworker panel allowed in the agreed access levels
Permission test results by access level
asks: Your Workfront administrator, to enable Coworker and change the settings with us
A test user at each access level that will use Coworker
risk: Coworker changing records a user should only read: we agree the tools and access levels first, and test each access level before planners start.
outcome: Your planners use Coworker inside Workfront within their own Planning permissions, with the agreed tools on and every change logged.

steps: Collect the tasks your planners do most often, such as creating records from a brief, updating fields and linking records.
Write a prompt for each task, noting which workspace, record type or record page to open first, since the panel works in that context.
Test each prompt on your own workspaces, and refine it until Coworker proposes the right action.
Teach your planners to review each proposed action before accepting it, using the tested prompts in a short session.
deliverables: Tested prompts for your planners' common tasks
Short guide on where to run each prompt
Planner training session
asks: The tasks your planners do most often in Workfront Planning
Time from a group of planners for testing and training
risk: Planners accepting an action without reading it: we teach the review step in training, using tested prompts, so each proposed change is checked before it is accepted.
outcome: Your planners create, update and link Planning records with tested Coworker prompts, and review each proposed action before accepting it.

steps: Agree with your marketing leads who manages campaigns, products and personas, and who only views them.
Set permissions on the GenStudio workspace in Workfront Planning, sharing it with the agreed users, teams or job roles and sharing views separately.
Add the fields your campaigns, products and personas need, and record each in a field list your planners can follow.
Make a test change in each product, and check that it shows in the other, for campaigns, products and personas.
deliverables: Permissions and sharing on the GenStudio workspace
Added fields for campaigns, products and personas
Two-way change test results
asks: Who should manage campaigns, products and personas, and who should only view them
The fields your teams need on campaigns, products and personas
risk: Changes in one product that do not show in the other, or edits by the wrong people: we set permissions first and test a change in each direction.
outcome: Your campaigns, products and personas are managed in Workfront Planning and stay in step with GenStudio for Performance Marketing, with the right people editing them.
